status: fixed before V9 calculations; descriptive analysis after V1-V8 development results were viewed
question: Do the six original observed inputs have temporally stable simple associations with next-day raw SRT returns, and do previously fitted fuzzy experts show repeatable local benefit?
boundary: Read only saved original windows, original development fold assignments, existing V1/V7 prediction and V7 expert-component files. Do not fit or tune any new model, change inputs/targets, use the final holdout, or rank new candidates.
feature_probe: For all six original feature channels, use only the last historical row of each 20-day window. In each of the three original folds report training and outer-validation Pearson/Spearman correlation with the next-day raw close log return. Split each feature at that fold's outer-training median and report high-minus-low next-return means on both train and validation using the same training threshold. Report all six features and all three folds; no cherry-picked significance claims.
volatility_probe: For original channel 2 (20-day SRT volatility), define high/low from each fold's outer-training median. Report state counts, mean and standard deviation of next-day raw returns in outer train versus validation. Within each state report Pearson association of SRT five-day momentum (channel 1) and STI one-day return (channel 3) with next-day SRT return. The two predictors are fixed for economic interpretability, not selected by validation scores.
saved_prediction_probe: On the same training-median volatility groups, score saved Z0, original V1 Fuzzy2 and V7 staged Gaussian forecasts on their original validation dates. V1/V7 scores are seed-specific; report seed-mean RMSE/MAE and counts, without treating seeds as independent market dates. Use saved V7 component files for the four fold/seed runs where the inner selection accepted a nonzero local term. For each Gaussian rule, define its high-activation region as alpha >= 0.8 and compare own versus other expert MAE on evaluation dates, labeling fewer than 20 dates as small descriptive regions.
interpretation: Correlations and median splits describe simple marginal relationships, not an upper bound on nonlinear information in the full 20x6 tensor. Expert-region errors are post-selection diagnostics, not a new test or a reason to select a model. Stable signs across viewed folds are descriptive only; multiple probes and repeated use of these folds preclude an independent significance claim.
outputs: feature correlations and median splits, volatility regime statistics and conditional associations, saved-model errors by regime, V7 expert-region comparisons, source hashes and a Chinese report. No new predictions or checkpoints.
